solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Prepare to give orders — or receive one?

definitions.meaning: to assume leadership so that you are the one issuing instructions
read literally, to be handed a single order, accepting an instruction from someone else

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether getting ready to boss others about really means being bossed.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading treats the phrase literally: you 'take' a 'command' when someone gives you an order, so 'one' refers back to orders.
explanation.definitionFit: Assuming control is the idiomatic sense; the literal sense is simply accepting a single instruction.

clue.text: After exam tucked into meal with a will

indicators.note: after places the eating piece behind the exam piece in the answer

parts.note: an exam is a test
someone who tucked into a meal ate it

explanation.surface: A student finishes an exam and eats heartily.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who dies having made a legal will is described in law as testate, the opposite of intestate.

clue.text: Gurkha kit includes uniform of this colour

indicators.note: includes signals that the answer sits inside the run of letters across the two words

explanation.surface: Gurkha soldiers' kit comes with a uniform in a certain shade.
explanation.definitionFit: The dull brownish-yellow cloth of army dress is named after its colour, and soldiers are said to wear it.

clue.text: Shouted as told to strike

definitions.meaning: to have yelled something out loud
a union calls workers out when it orders them to strike

explanation.surface: A union official bellowed the order for the workers to walk out.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are standard phrasal-verb senses: one of crying out, the other of a union summoning workers to industrial action.

clue.text: Graduate elected as principal

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts, a graduate
a candidate who is elected is in

explanation.surface: A university graduate becomes head teacher by election.
explanation.definitionFit: Main and principal are synonyms meaning chief or most important.

clue.text: A confused Crimean statesman, perhaps

indicators.note: confused tells us the letters of these words are muddled into a new order

explanation.surface: A muddled politician from the Crimea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'statesman' is read as a man from the States, a citizen of the USA; 'perhaps' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A man of the United States can whimsically be called a States-man, so the nationality fits by example.

clue.text: Boring bit of exercise

definitions.meaning: the bit of a power tool used for boring holes
a repeated routine practice, such as parade-ground training

explanation.surface: A dull spell of physical exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the tool for making holes and a disciplined training routine.

clue.text: Places visited on holidays, or between holidays

indicators.note: between puts the little word inside the second holidays piece

parts.note: holidays are rests, breaks from work
taken as written

explanation.surface: Trips to holiday spots, either during the holiday or in the gaps between.
explanation.definitionFit: Seaside and ski towns that tourists flock to are holiday resorts.

clue.text: For now it's set at Greenwich

definitions.meaning: in the interim, as in the phrase 'in the ...'
Greenwich ... is the time standard fixed at the Greenwich observatory in London

explanation.surface: A temporary clock setting is fixed at the Greenwich observatory.
explanation.definitionFit: The interim period until something happens, and the mean solar time used as the Greenwich reference, share the spelling.

clue.text: Working steam mill of no great importance

indicators.note: working means the letters are worked over into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A steam-driven mill that is still running but insignificant.
explanation.definitionFit: Small-time describes an operator or business that is minor and unimportant.

clue.text: Turn aside for inspiration

indicators.note: turn tells us the following word's letters are turned around into another arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone steps off the path looking for a creative spark.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is singular but the answer is plural; inspiration in the collective sense covers a stock of thoughts.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspiration in the mass sense means creative thoughts, the stuff a brainstorm produces.

clue.text: Stays with sailor on a date in Rome

indicators.note: in a down light 'on' would put one piece over another; here it simply joins the sailor to the date

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman
the Ides was a fixed date in the Roman calendar, the 15th or 13th of the month

explanation.surface: A tourist lingers with a seaman on a romantic evening in Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: To abide is to remain or dwell somewhere, so stays is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Rubbish-holder in container ship

parts.note: a bin is a container
a liner is a large passenger ship

explanation.surface: Garbage stored aboard a container vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A plastic sack lining a dustbin holds the household rubbish.

clue.text: Acting as a unit providing some wooden blocks

indicators.note: providing some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A team works together supplying timber blocks.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means all together as one body, a group acting collectively.

clue.text: Chelsea versus Bath?

parts.note: Chelsea buns and Bath buns are British cakes, so a contest between them is a fight of buns

explanation.surface: A football club playing a rugby side.
explanation.walkthrough: Chelsea suggests the London football club and Bath the rugby club, but both are also names of sweet British buns; a 'bun fight' is also slang for a tea party or squabble.
explanation.definitionFit: Taken literally, a clash between two kinds of bun; idiomatically, a noisy party or petty row.

clue.text: Fifty per cent of wisecrackers may be fools

parts.note: fifty per cent is a half
people who make clever jokes are wits

explanation.surface: Half of all jokers could turn out to be idiots.
explanation.definitionFit: Dim or foolish people are insultingly called halfwits, as if possessing only part of their wits.

clue.text: It's not true oil, in fact, needs changing

indicators.note: needs changing tells us the letters of the words before must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone claims that the oil, in reality, should be replaced.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a phrase about something invented; the adjective fits a sentence like 'the story is not true'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something invented or made up for a story is not real, the opposite of factual.

clue.text: Playboy lifestyle — but you get nothing for nothing?

parts.note: something you get for nothing is free
love means nil or zero in tennis scoring

explanation.surface: A womaniser's way of life, though there is no such thing as a free lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nothing for nothing' echoes the proverb; read in pieces, 'nothing' gives the tennis score and 'for nothing' gives the costless word.
explanation.definitionFit: A playboy enjoys casual sexual relations without commitment, the 1960s ideal of unbound romance.

clue.text: It could result in deflation being on the way

definitions.text: It could result in deflation being on the way

parts.words: It could result in deflation being on the way
parts.note: a tyre that gets a hole while driving along the road goes flat, which sounds like an economics warning

explanation.surface: An economist warns that falling prices are coming.
explanation.walkthrough: Deflation reads as economic falling prices, but here it is a tyre losing air while you are on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A hole in a tyre lets the air escape so it deflates during the journey.

clue.text: Trains for smokers?

definitions.meaning: old steam locomotives, so called for the clouds they emit
people who draw on cigarettes or pipes

explanation.surface: Railway carriages where tobacco may be used.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes both chugging steam locomotives and people who smoke.

clue.text: Second best part in hilarious performance

parts.note: the cream is the best part of something

explanation.surface: An actor has the second-best role in a comic show.
explanation.definitionFit: Something extremely funny is informally called a scream.

clue.text: One who painted the heartless Dickensian doctor

parts.note: Edouard Manet was a French Impressionist painter

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter of the little word is cut out

explanation.surface: A painter portrayed a cruel doctor from Dickens.
explanation.walkthrough: Doctor Manette is the prisoner of the Bastille in Dickens's A Tale of Two Cities.
explanation.definitionFit: Dr Alexandre Manette is a central character in A Tale of Two Cities by Charles Dickens.

clue.text: Cow appears as appropriate in marshland

indicators.note: in puts the fitting piece inside the marshland piece

parts.note: a fen is low marshy land, as in the East Anglian Fens
appropriate means right, fitting

explanation.surface: A cow turns up properly in the boggy fields.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cow' looks like a noun for the animal in the marsh, but it is the verb meaning to intimidate.
explanation.definitionFit: To cow someone is to intimidate or scare them into submission.

clue.text: Silent comedy film star

parts.note: the Marx Brother who never spoke on screen, communicating by mime and a horn

explanation.surface: A star of the silent-movie era of comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Silent' suggests silent-era films, but this comic made talking pictures and simply never spoke in them.
explanation.definitionFit: The harp-playing Marx brother kept mute in all his films, so he was the silent one of the team.

clue.text: 50 is 10? Pay attention!

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
ten written out

explanation.surface: A teacher snaps at a pupil who says fifty equals ten.
explanation.definitionFit: Listen is a command to attend closely, the same as telling someone to pay attention.

clue.text: The point of growing roses

parts.note: read literally, the sharp point that grows on a rose stem

explanation.surface: A gardener asks why anyone bothers cultivating roses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'point' reads as purpose, but it means a sharp spike that grows on rose bushes.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharp spike on a rose stem is literally a point that grows on the plant.

clue.text: Attempt to assassinate?

definitions.meaning: to have a go at something
to kill with a knife, one way of murdering a target

explanation.surface: An assassination bid.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a try and a knife thrust, the latter a way to murder.

clue.text: Medium for broadcasting three dances

indicators.note: dances suggests the letters of the word jig about into a new order

explanation.surface: A radio channel airs three dance numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: Radio and television are said to go out over the airwaves, the old notion of a medium carrying waves.

clue.text: Definitely caught and bowled

definitions.note: an adverb in the clue, while the answer is usually an adjective meaning complete; the swap works in 'definitely a rogue'

parts.note: in cricket a batsman who is caught is out
taken as written
in cricket a batsman who is bowled is also out

explanation.surface: A cricket commentator confirms that a batsman was caught and bowled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caught and bowled' is a single cricket dismissal where the bowler takes the catch; here each half separately gives the word for dismissed.
explanation.definitionFit: Out-and-out means complete or thoroughgoing, as in 'an out-and-out villain', which is definitely a villain.

clue.text: A lover can be excited and lose equilibrium

indicators.note: excited tells us the letters of these words are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: An aroused lover can get so worked up as to topple over.
explanation.definitionFit: To topple because your weight is too far to one side is to lose your balance.
